title: Kernel residency and latency decomposition - microtrace analysis
body:
Summary:
This note captures an ad-hoc investigation into an intermittent tail-latency pattern we observed on the 8xA100 single-node serving cluster. The symptom: periodic 10-30ms spikes on p99 for short-decoder workloads (seq_len <= 128) that correlate with sudden drops in SM occupancy followed by a wave of small kernel re-entries. Goal is to stitch together Nsight captures, CUDA graph replay artifacts, and microtrace timelines to produce an actionable hypothesis and short experiments list.

Context and why this matters:
- Workload: short-decoder chat endpoints with aggressive batching (microbatch size 8, dynamic batching window 6ms).
- SLA: p99 < 80ms. Observed p99 spikes up to 130ms under steady QPS.
- Prior mitigations (in prod): slight increase in batch horizon, KV cache warmup, priority boosting for control streams. Spikes persist sporadically.

Experiment/trace setup:
- Node: 8xA100-SXM4, CUDA 12.4, driver 545.x, Nsight Systems 2029.1.
- Capture: full-system Nsight timeline (60s captures) + driver-level kernel timestamps. Enabled NVTX around batch ingress and each sub-kernel (matmul, softmax, rotary, layernorm).
- Repro: synthetic replay harness that replays real traffic traces at 1.2x peak QPS to increase incidence of spike occurrences.
- Measurement vectors: per-kernel duration, SM occupancy (sampled), kernel launch latency (CPU -> driver submit delay), CUDA graph replay jitter, and host-side scheduling gaps.

Quick observations from Nsight captures:
- On each p99 spike occurrence we saw a short idle pocket (~200-350us) across a subset of SMs while other SMs remain busy. This results in an imbalanced occupancy map where overall occupancy metric drops by ~7-12% for a 1ms window.
- Immediately after the pocket, there is a burst of very short kernels (~5-20us) that appear to be re-entering previously suspended CUDA Graph segments. These short kernels are not present in baseline steady-state traces.
- NVTX spans indicate the pause happens between end-of-kv-prefetch and start-of-decoder-matmul for affected requests.
- Host-side trace shows small spikes in kernel launch latency (driver queue latency) that align with occupancy drop window (+40-120us).

CUDA Graph / Replay findings:
- Graph-based replay of the same batch sequence on an isolated environment reproduces the micro-pocket only when the host submits graphs with mixed priority streams (PIO) and when graph reuse is enabled.
- Disabling graph reuse eliminates the short re-entry kernels but increases average latency slightly due to repeated graph construction.
- Inspecting graph capture fragments shows conditional edges for small memory prefetch kernels that are sometimes elided during capture but re-instantiated during replay due to allocator alignment differences. This causes fractionally different kernel ordering and occasional preemption-like replays.

Hypothesis (summary):
We think a combination of: (1) mixed-priority stream scheduling, (2) graph reuse coupled with allocator-induced capture variance, and (3) host-side submit jitter creates transient SM underutilization pockets. The runtime then issues several very short kernels to reconcile state (e.g., re-apply prefetch/housekeeping kernels), which amplifies tail latency for requests that land into that window.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- Removing graph reuse -> no short re-entry kernels in Nsight timeline.
- Forcing single-priority stream -> reduced incidence of occupancy pockets in synthetic replay.
- Aligning allocator policy (forcing deterministic capture addresses) reduced the ordering variance seen when comparing capture vs replay.

Counter-evidence / open questions:
- Not all spikes are explained by graph reuse; some captured pockets occur with no graph operations in-flight (pure kernel launches).
- NVLINK-host DMA timing occasionally shows bursty DMA completion that slightly precedes the pocket; causality unclear.
- On multi-tenant nodes we see stronger effects; is interference from co-located NVLINK/DMA activity exacerbating SM wakeup?

Microtrace excerpts (timestamp progression from a representative capture):
- 00:12.345.100 host submit batch-A
- 00:12.345.148 KV-prefetch kernel (SM occ=82%)
- 00:12.345.250 small host submit jitter spike (+85us)
- 00:12.345.268 observed SM pocket start (SM occ drops to 71%)
- 00:12.345.420 burst of short kernels (4 x 8-16us) labelled "graph_housekeeping"
- 00:12.345.430 decoder-matmul resumes (SM occ back to 84%)
- 00:12.345.465 request completion -> +22ms on request latency vs baseline

Short experiments to validate quickly (order matters):
1) Reproduce with graph reuse disabled in staging: measure p99 over 1 hour. Expect reduction in incidence if hypothesis holds.
2) Run with single CUDA stream priority for inference-only streams (no mixed PIO): compare occupancy variance.
3) Force deterministic allocator addresses during capture and replay: check kernel ordering diffs.
4) Add small host-side pacing (10-30us smoothing) to reduce submit bursts.
5) On multi-tenant nodes, temporarily throttle NVLINK DMA from background tenants and check effect.

Cost / risk tradeoffs:
- Disabling graph reuse reduces throughput efficiency (extra capture cost and CPU overhead) — may increase cost on heavy workloads. But low-effort and high-confidence way to remove one variable.
- Smoothing host submits may be low-risk but requires care in scheduler integration to avoid increasing median latency.

Implementation notes and quick commands used:
- Nsight system capture command (used): nsys profile --output=run-2029-03-22 --trace=cuda,cudnn --capture-range=stop-on-range-end --sample=%5
- CUDA graph replay harness: ./replay_harness --trace-file traces/short-decoder-2029-03.json --graph-reuse=on --allocator=default
- Deterministic allocator flag used for test: --allocator=fixed-base-0x700000000
- Quick script to extract kernel durations from Nsight .qdrep: ./scripts/nsight-extract-kernels.py run-2029-03-22.qdrep --filter "graph_housekeeping|decoder-matmul" > kernels.csv

Immediate actions (next 2 weeks):
- Run Experiment 1 & 2 in staging (Aisha + Ravi) and collect p50/p95/p99 distributions (deadline: 2029-04-05).
- If experiments reduce incidence by >50%, draft rollout plan to canary change graph_reuse=false for one Dedicated cluster (Clara to coordinate with infra).
- Create a low-overhead host pacing prototype in runtime scheduler (10us bucketed smoothing) for A/B testing.
- Log follow-ups for NVLINK DMA correlation and multi-tenant interference (RCA ticket JIRA-RT-1193).

Notes to self / crumbs:
- Look up earlier note about "graph fragment elision" (confluence link above) — might be related to allocator alignment.
- Check device driver release notes for any 'sm-wakeup' related bug fixes around 2028-12.

Appendix: quick table of metrics observed (representative)
- steady avg sm occupancy: 83%
- occupancy during pocket: 71%
- pocket duration: 0.2 - 0.35 ms
- number of short re-entry kernels seen: 3 - 6 (5-20us each)
- p99 spike magnitude: +30 - 55 ms over baseline

Related artifacts and traces (local):
- /mnt/traces/run-2029-03-22.qdrep
- /mnt/replays/short-decoder-2029-03-replay.log

End of note.

If you have ideas or see an obvious missing test, please add comments inline in the doc or ping in #eng-serving-runtime.
